ca_avalanche_wall.blurb: Avalanche Wall is a small crag in Pine Creek Canyon above Bishop, in the Eastern Sierra, at about 7,200 feet. It holds seven routes, a blend of trad and sport lines that run from a single pitch up to three. Grades start at 5.9 and reach into the 5.12 range, with the bulk around 5.10 and 5.11. The wall can be seen from the road but is hidden from the roadside pullouts, so the way up is a long walk along a big gully and then a cairned path uphill, roughly half an hour in all.

ca_aeroperro_wall.blurb: Aeroperro Wall is one of the small cliffs in Children's Forest, in the Keller Peak area of the San Bernardino Mountains at roughly 7,100 feet. The wall faces northwest, so it only picks up sun late in the afternoon, and trees at its foot shade the belay spot. It is steep for its size. There are seven routes, four trad and three sport. The trad lines range from an easy Class 2 scramble to about 5.10, while the sport climbs sit between 5.10 and 5.11. To get there, cross beneath the power lines from the Children's Forest trail and follow the drainage down until it pinches in.

ca_carmel_meadows_beach_boulders.blurb: These are seven boulder problems scattered along the sand at Carmel Meadows, a short stretch of coast south of Carmel-by-the-Sea. The boulders lie a little farther along the beach from the main Carmel Meadows blocks, and the stairs from the trailhead bring you down to them in about five minutes. Problems run from V1 to V4, with most at V2 and V3. Landings are mostly sand, which is kinder than at the neighbouring Southern Spire. Rock quality varies: some of it is loose, but much is solid and abrasive on the fingertips.

ca_chuckwalla_needle.blurb: Chuckwalla Needle is a pointed formation on the Fairview skyline, within the Middle Earth section of Fairview Mountain near Apple Valley in the High Desert, at about 3,800 feet. It has a summit worth topping out on and a long, broken wall that carries several routes. There are seven in total, five sport and two trad, spanning 5.8 to 5.11 with most in the 5.9 to 5.11 range. To reach the base, scramble up the gully behind The Owl, traverse across from Hungover Wall, or finish another route on the formation and come down to it.
